messages:
jdoe (Acme): Hey, hitting a reproducible issue with streaming responses. The model returns partial JSON and then the stream cuts off, no finish_reason and no [DONE].

jdoe (Acme): Happens on our prod client when responses are ~1.5k tokens. Client shows network still open but no more events.

jdoe (Acme): Example payload we receive (truncated):
```
data: {\"id\":\"resp_123\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"...\"}}] }

data: {\"id\":\"resp_123\",\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"...\"}}] }
```

jdoe (Acme): After that, nothing. No `data: [DONE]`, no event with finish reason.

maria (Support): Thanks for the report — I'll repro. Is this using the hosted API or a Dedicated instance?

jdoe (Acme): Hosted API in us-west1. Using SSE endpoint with `Accept: text/event-stream`.

maria (Support): Any proxies in front of the client? CDN?

jdoe (Acme): No CDN. Direct client -> our backend -> Redwood. We tested bypassing our backend and same happens from a raw curl.

jdoe (Acme): Curl repro we used: 
```bash
curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \\
  \"https://api.redwood.com/v1/responses/stream?model=rw1\"
```

josh (Infra): tagging infra — does this look like a connection teardown on our side?

alice (SRE): Can you grab the raw TCP/HTTP logs + ids? We want the response headers and connection close semantics.

jdoe (Acme): Attaching a short capture from curl (client-side):
```
> GET /v1/responses/stream?model=rw1 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.com
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer ***

< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< x-request-id: req_987654

< data: {\"id\":\"resp_123\",\"choices\":...}
< data: {\"id\":\"resp_123\",\"choices\":...}
# then nothing for >30s, connection still open from curl perspective, no more data
```

josh (Infra): Ok `transfer-encoding: chunked` and connection remains open. That suggests the server hasn't sent the final chunk. Could be process crash or runtime abort without proper teardown.

maria (Support): Can you share the request body you used? Any `max_tokens`, `stream` flags, or stop sequences we should know about?

jdoe (Acme): Payload: 
```json
{\"model\":\"rw1\",\"input\":\"<long prompt>\",\"max_tokens\":2048,\"stream\":true}
```

josh (Infra): Thanks. I'm going to check runtimes for `req_987654`. alice, can you watch for runtime OOMs or GPU preemption around that time window?

alice (SRE): Watching. Also check our runtime logs — maybe the worker process sent a small TCP RST that the client didn't surface.

devex-bot: New log search job started for `req_987654` across us-west1 clusters.

maria (Support): In the meantime can you try a couple of quick repros: 1) set `max_tokens` smaller (like 512) 2) set `stream` false to see if non-stream responses finish fine

jdoe (Acme): Good idea. Non-stream returns a full complete JSON no problem. Smaller stream seems to complete for shorter outputs, but cutoff consistently when expected >1k tokens.

alice (SRE): Found worker logs for req_987654: `Runtime: generate loop exited unexpectedly: write to connection failed: broken pipe` at 2026-02-28T14:34:12Z. Right before that we have several GC pauses reported.

josh (Infra): Broken pipe likely when client closed or connection error. But client says connection remained open. Could be an intermediary dropping idle streams. Any LB logs?

alice (SRE): Load balancer logs show a long-lived TCP connection with no termination. No LB health checks triggered. But I see the backend returned a 200 then no more bytes for ~30s then the backend process restarted (OOM killer) at 2026-02-28T14:34:40Z. That matches.

maria (Support): If worker OOMed, we should have server-side partial writes but no final [DONE]. That matches the symptom. Two action items: provide mitigations for the customer (client-side reconnect + resume) and escalate to runtime to reduce memory for streaming and/or use chunked generation.

jdoe (Acme): Client reconnect/resume is tricky — we rely on idempotent session resumes. Does Redwood support resuming a stream from a partial KV cache or last token?

josh (Infra): At the moment we don't provide an official resume for streaming responses. We have fallbacks: 1) run non-stream with higher reliability 2) pin lower max_tokens or split request 3) increase Dedicated capacity. But we should add a documented retry pattern for incomplete streams.

alice (SRE): For immediate customer mitigation: try `max_tokens` < 1024 OR chunk prompt into multiple sequential calls storing KV/prefix. Also add client-side logic: if SSE connection drops mid-response, treat as transient and re-request full non-stream or call a shorter non-stream to finish the content.

maria (Support): I'll send a guidance email with repro and mitigation. Also escalating to runtime team to add memory safeguards and ensure final `[DONE]` is flushed even on worker termination when possible.

jdoe (Acme): Appreciate that. One more weird detail: the truncated JSON sometimes ends inside an object (malformed JSON) which breaks our parser. Any quick tips to make our parser robust?

alice (SRE): Yes — treat stream frames as discrete events and implement a lenient aggregator: only parse complete braced objects, buffer partial text until next event, and on reconnect if you detect an incomplete object do not attempt to parse until you re-fetch final chunk or fall back to non-stream. Also watch for `finish_reason` presence — if missing, trigger fallback.

jdoe (Acme): Got it. We'll implement a simple aggregator and fallback to non-stream when `finish_reason` absent after timeout.

maria (Support): I'll follow up with runtime owner for ETA on the fix. For tracking: support ticket #324.

devex-bot: Escalation created: runtime-team (priority: high) — issue: worker OOM causing truncated streams (support#324).

josh (Infra): For the runtime team — propose: enable periodic flush of final event on SIGTERM, add memory limits per generation, and add metrics for partial-stream counts.

alice (SRE): Also recommend adding `x-stream-final: pending|flushed` header (internal only) so we can debug if final flush succeeded.

maria (Support): Thanks everyone. jdoe — we'll keep you updated in this thread and follow up by email with the mitigation steps and repro summary.

jdoe (Acme): Thanks all. Implementing client-side fallback now. Will report back if still failing. :thumbsup:
